commitResults.messageTitle: Level-0: Rename, greet and exit
Add support for echo
Add task storage and list command
Add ability to mark tasks as done and undone
Use a Task class to represent tasks
Add Todo, Deadline, Event class
Extract command handling out of main()
commitResults.messageBody:
main() had grown to 78 lines and operated at several levels of
abstraction at once: it drove the read-eval-print loop, split raw
input strings, indexed into the task array, and formatted output.
This violates both "Avoid Long Methods" and "SLAP Hard" from the
course code quality guidelines, and it forced a reader interested in
one command to scan the whole method to find it.

Break it up into short methods that each sit at a single level of
abstraction. main() is now 17 lines and reads as a summary of the
program: greet, loop over commands, farewell. executeCommand()
dispatches to one focused method per command, and task construction
moves into createTask()/createDeadline()/createEvent().

Three further issues fall out of the same change:

- The "Got it. I've added this task" block was copy-pasted across the
  todo, deadline and event cases. Those cases now share one branch
  that delegates to createTask() and printTaskAdded(), removing the
  duplication ("Minimise Code Duplication").
- A commented-out default branch was left over from Level-2. It is
  deleted rather than carried into the new methods ("Delete Dead
  Code"); git history retains it if it is ever needed.
- The counter named "index" actually held the number of tasks, and
  "description" held a description-and-time pair. Renamed to
  taskCount and descriptionAndTimes ("Avoid Misleading Names").

mark/unmark now use guard clauses so the normal path is not nested
inside an if ("Make the Happy Path Prominent"), and their shared
bounds check is named isExistingTask().

Behaviour is unchanged: old and new versions produce byte-identical
output for a script exercising all six commands and an out-of-range
task number.

commitResults.messageTitle: Follow the coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
The Java coding standard requires K&R brace style: the opening brace
sits on the same line as the declaration, separated by a space. The
four task classes were inconsistent about this, writing `getType(){`
in ten places while Task and Event used `class X {` correctly on
their declarations.

Insert the missing space so brace style is uniform across the
codebase, satisfying the "Follow a Standard" guideline: a reader
should not be able to tell which parts were typed on which day.

Whitespace only; no behaviour or logic is affected.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add YuWeiException for invalid user input
commitResults.messageBody: Unrecognised commands were silently ignored, so the user got no feedback that their input was wrong. Catching the exception in the main loop rather than inside executeCommand() means later increments can report input errors just by throwing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject commands with missing or blank arguments
commitResults.messageBody: Typing a command with nothing after it crashed the bot with an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, and a description of only spaces was accepted as a valid task. One guard method handles both, so each command can supply its own message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Validate deadline and event argument formats
commitResults.messageBody: A deadline without /by, or an event missing /from or /to, indexed past the end of the split array and crashed the bot out of the main loop. Check each split before use and report the expected format so the user can correct the input.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report invalid task numbers via YuWeiException
commitResults.messageBody: mark and unmark crashed on non-numeric input, and reported an out-of-range number by printing directly rather than through the error path used by every other command. Parse and range-check in one helper that throws, so both cases reach the main loop's handler and printTaskNotFound is no longer needed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject new tasks when the list is full
commitResults.messageBody: Adding a 101st task wrote past the end of the fixed-size array and crashed the bot. Check the count before constructing the task, and build the message from MAX_TASKS so it stays accurate if the limit changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix comment and message formatting
commitResults.messageBody: A missing space in an if condition, a Javadoc summary without a terminating period, a stray blank comment line, and one error message inconsistent with the others.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-5'
Organise classes into packages
commitResults.messageBody: All six classes sat in the default package, which does not scale and gives no indication of how they relate. Group them by responsibility: yuwei for the chatbot and its exception, yuwei.task for the task hierarchy. No visibility changes were needed, since the task classes' protected members are used only by their siblings in the same package.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-Packages'
Store tasks in an ArrayList instead of a fixed array
commitResults.messageBody: An ArrayList resizes itself and tracks its own size, so the MAX_TASKS limit and manual taskCount bookkeeping are no longer needed. This also makes deleting tasks straightforward.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add delete command
commitResults.messageBody: Lets users remove a task by its list number. Reuses parseTaskIndex so invalid numbers get the same error messages as mark/unmark.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add toFileString to tasks for saving to disk
commitResults.messageBody:
Level-7 needs tasks written to a data file. Each task type knows its own fields, so each one formats itself as a line (e.g. D | 0 | return book | June 6th). This keeps the upcoming saving code free of instanceof checks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Save tasks to disk and load them on startup
commitResults.messageBody:
Level-7 requires tasks to survive a restart. A new Storage class writes the list to ./data/yuwei.txt after every command, so no change is lost, and reads it back when the app starts. The path is relative and built with Path.of so it works on other computers and OSes. Corrupted lines are skipped with a warning rather than discarding the whole file, and a missing file or folder is treated as a first run.

The data folder is gitignored because it holds personal task data, not source code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Make task output formatting consistent
commitResults.messageBody:
The "task added" messages were printed without the 5-space indent
used by every other message, so they stood out against the dividers.
Task descriptions were also printed flush against their date details,
e.g. "return book(by: June 6th)".

Let's indent the "task added" messages like the other messages, show
the added task on its own line as the mark/unmark/delete messages do,
and add a space before the "(by:" and "(from:" details.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Ui, Parser and TaskList from YuWei
commitResults.messageBody:
YuWei did everything in static methods: printing messages, splitting
command strings and managing the task list. Changing any one of these
meant editing the same large class, and the ArrayList of tasks could be
modified from anywhere without its index checks.

Let's give each responsibility its own class:
* Ui: all reading of input and printing of messages
* Parser: turning command text into task numbers and Task objects
* TaskList: the list of tasks, validating task numbers in one place
  and exposing only a read-only view of its contents

YuWei becomes an object that holds a Ui, Storage and TaskList and
coordinates them, following the structure suggested for A-MoreOOP.

Parser's methods stay static because it holds no state. Tasks are
still loaded after the greeting, so file problems are reported under
it as before. The chatbot's output is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Store deadline dates as LocalDate
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadlines stored their date as whatever text the user typed, so the
chatbot could not tell "2019-10-15" was a date or show it consistently.

Let's store it as a java.time.LocalDate instead:
* Parser reads dates in yyyy-mm-dd format and rejects anything else,
  including impossible dates such as 2019-02-30
* Deadline shows dates as "MMM dd yyyy", e.g. "Oct 15 2019", using an
  English locale so month names are the same on every computer
* Storage saves dates as yyyy-mm-dd and reads them back as LocalDate

Deadlines saved in the old free-text format cannot be read as dates,
so Storage now reports them as corrupted lines and skips them.

Event start and end times are left as text, as Level-8 only requires
deadlines to use dates.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command to search task descriptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Users had no way to look up a task other than scanning the whole list,
which gets slow as the list grows.

Let's add "find KEYWORD", which shows the tasks whose description
contains the keyword. The search ignores case, so "find BOOK" matches
"read book". TaskList returns the matches as a new list, leaving the
task list itself unchanged, and Ui says so when nothing matches.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JavaDoc comments to remaining classes and methods
commitResults.messageBody:
Task, its subclasses, YuWeiException and YuWei.main() had no header
comments, so their purpose had to be worked out from the code.

Let's add JavaDoc comments to them, so that every non-private class,
method and field is documented. The javadoc tool now reports no
undocumented items and no syntax errors.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace template user guide with YuWei's guide
commitResults.messageBody:
docs/README.md still contained the project template's placeholder
text, so the product website gave users no help with the chatbot.

Let's write a user guide covering every command: its format, an
example, and the output it gives, taken from real runs of the
chatbot. Add a quick start section, an explanation of the task
symbols, where tasks are saved, and a command summary table.

The guide also covers the find command and yyyy-mm-dd deadline dates,
which are added by the Level-8 and Level-9 branches.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
